messages:
Maria Chen: Hey team — uploaded the SSE vs WS vs non-stream sweep charts for H100/A100/T4 across us-west1/eu-west1. TL;DR: streaming gives p50 latency win at low concurrency but loses throughput at high batch sizes. Link: https://storage.redwood-internal/reports/sweep-1802468101.pdf
Kevin Cho: taking a look now. are those runs with flash-attn enabled?
Maria Chen: yes for H100 we toggled flash-attn on/off; A100 runs used optimized cuBLAS kernels. T4 used standard kernels + int8 quant.
Samir Patel: can you paste the key numbers? small bullets ok.
Maria Chen: p50/p95/p99 (ms) @ 1k tokens/req, concurrency 16:
- H100 streaming (flash-attn): p50 45, p95 120, p99 300; throughput 620 tok/s
- H100 non-stream (batched HTTP): p50 85, p95 160, p99 420; throughput 1100 tok/s
- A100 streaming: p50 60, p95 150, p99 380; throughput 450 tok/s
- T4 non-stream quantized: p50 140, p95 300, p99 900; throughput 300 tok/s
Jen Brown: interesting that non-stream higher throughput on H100. suggests batching path is winning on kernel selection.
Kevin Cho: exactly. streaming keeps tokens flowing but batching aggregates kernels -> better utilization. also KV cache access pattern differs so memory bandwidth matters.
SRE Oncall: any regional differences? we need to size pools per region for Dedicated.
Maria Chen: yes — us-west1 shows ~10% better throughput vs eu-west1 on A100 due to interconnect and kernel performance; H100 diff ~4%. Charts in the PDF have per-region heatmaps.
Samir Patel: for Dedicated sizing I propose: start with H100 pools sized for 1000 concurrent streaming users = 60 GPUs in us-west1, simulate fallback to non-stream if throughput needs spike.
Jen Brown: can we add a config snippet to reproduce the test?
Maria Chen: sure, here's the client harness we used:
```bash
# streaming test (ws)
python load_test.py --model rdl-7b --mode streaming --concurrency 16 --seq 1024 --region us-west1 --gpu h100 --flash-attn true
# non-stream (http batch)
python load_test.py --model rdl-7b --mode nonstream --concurrency 128 --batch 32 --seq 1024 --region us-west1 --gpu h100 --quant none
```
Kevin Cho: perf note: when batch>16 on H100, p50 drops but p95/p99 widen drastically unless we enable dynamic KV cache sharding.
Maria Chen: good call — dynamic sharding reduced p99 by ~30% in a follow-up. I'll add that to the appendix.
SRE Oncall: can someone create a follow-up ticket to evaluate fallback policies (stream->nonstream) when queue depth > X? want to avoid SLA surprises.
Jen Brown: @Maria Chen can you add a recommended threshold and config for automatic fallback? maybe queue depth 64 or latency above 250ms p95? :thinking_face: 
Maria Chen: will do. initial recommendation: fallback when in-flight requests > 48 OR p95 > 220ms for two consecutive minutes. I'll attach the suggested rollout config in the ticket.
infra-bot: Created ticket INF-4321: "Evaluate stream->nonstream fallback policy + capacity sizing" assigned to Maria Chen.
Kevin Cho: one more thought — consider quantized non-stream variants for T4 pools to close throughput gap. accuracy tradeoff needs evals though.
Samir Patel: noted. we should run quality regressions as a separate sweep but keep perf matrix aligned so we can present cost/latency curves.
Maria Chen: thanks all. I'll update the PDF with dynamic-shard runs and open INF-4321 with the configs + charts. tagging this thread for follow-up in next eng-ml sync. :white_check_mark:
